figures.caption: FIGURE 1 Structural and electronic modulation of Li2S through Zr4+ substitution. (a) COMSOL simulations of the electronic/ionic conductivity influences within the active phase on the electrochemical reaction overpotential in all-solid-state lithium sulfide cathodes. (b) Schematic illustration showing the lattice and band structure evolution from pristine Li2S (left) to Zr4+ modified Li2S (right). In pristine Li2S, the wide bandgap and limited Li+ mobility result in poor electronic and ionic conductivities. Upon Zr4+ substitution for Li+, lattice expansion and the formation of abundant Li vacancies provide widened diffusion channels for Li+ transport. Simultaneously, Zr─S orbital hybridization introduces metal-induced gap states that narrow the bandgap and enhance electronic conduction. (c) Ionic radii of tetravalent metal cations across the fourth and fifth periods.

FIGURE 2 Mixed ionic and electronic conductivity activation for Li2S. (a) Correlation between Li2S-M (M = Mo, Sn, Zr) ionic radii and their ionic conductivities. (b) Rietveld refinement of the XRD pattern for ZLS-0.2. (c) HRTEM result of ZLS-0.2. (d,e) EPR and longitudinal relaxation time plots of ZLS-n (n = 0, 0.1, 0.2). (f) Density of states calculation result of Zr-doping Li2S. (g) Electronic conductivities of ZLS-n (n = 0, 0.1, 0.2). (h) UV–vis spectra of ZLS-n (n = 0, 0.1, 0.2) and their corresponding bandgaps. (i) Raman spectra of ZrS2, ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2.

FIGURE 3 Simulation results of solid-state conversion behavior for mixed ion-electron conductive Li2S. (a–h) Electron (a,e) and ion (c,g) transport pathways in the solid-state cathodes obtained from COMSOL simulations, along with the corresponding current density distributions for electron (b,f) and ion (d,h). (i) Electron transport tortuosities and corresponding conductivities within the ZLS-n (n = 0, 0.1 and 0.2) cathodes. (j) Ion transport tortuosities and corresponding conductivities within the ZLS-n (n = 0, 0.1 and 0.2) cathodes.

FIGURE 4 Experimental verification of solid-state conversion behavior for mixed ion-electron conductive Li2S. (a) DRT analyses of ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2 cathodes during charging process. (b,c) In situ XRD analyses of ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2 cathodes during cycling. (d,e) XPS analyses of ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2 cathodes during cycling.

FIGURE 5 Electrochemical performance of ASSLSBs with mixed ion-electron conductive Li2S. (a) Cycling performance ASSLSBs at current density of 0.5 mA cm−2 with Li2S loading of 1 mg cm−2. (b) EPR analysis of ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2 cathodes before and after 100 cycles. (c–f) DRT and XPS analyses of ZLS-0 and ZLS-0.2 cathodes across various cycle numbers. (g) Cycling performance of ASSLSBs with 65 wt.% Li2S cathodes. (h) Performance comparison between this work and previously reported ASSLSBs [3, 9, 11, 13–15, 28, 29].
